subject: Re: Altair Health — Azure Private Plan: delivery windows, SLA credits & escrow
messages:
From: Dana Reed <dana.reed@altairhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@altairhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Altair Health — Private Plan: delivery windows & escrow questions

Markus,

Thanks for the call earlier. A few follow-ups from our procurement and legal teams as we evaluate the Azure private plan offer:

1) Delivery windows / activation timeline
- We need confirmation of the typical lead time from PO to capacity activation for a 6 GPU reserved pool (US-West region). Our go-live target is 2027-01-15, so we need to understand milestones and what accelerators (expedited provisioning) exist.

2) SLA credits calculation and cap
- Our legal wants the exact formula for service credits (per-instance vs per-tenant) and whether there is a monthly cap. We also need the remedy timeline for incidents impacting inference latency.

3) Escrow and IP access
- We have a standard requirement to put a copy of the serving runtime (or an escrowed build) with a neutral escrow agent if certain continuity triggers occur. Is Redwood willing to do code escrow or a binary escrow with an agent?

4) Billing / invoicing cadence
- PO-based monthly invoice is preferred. Do you accept net-45? Any limitations on split invoicing for multi-sku commitments?

Attached: ALT_RFP_Qs.xlsx (list of procurement items)

Can you please respond with short bullets for procurement/legal and we'll circulate to our counsel? Happy to set a 30-min sync with our contracts manager if helpful.

Thanks,

Dana Reed
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Altair Health Systems
Dana.Reed@altairhealth.com

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Dana Reed <dana.reed@altairhealth.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Altair Health — Private Plan: delivery windows & escrow questions

Dana — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing answers below; I kept it concise for procurement/legal review. Happy to hop on with your contracts manager.

1) Delivery windows / activation timeline
- Typical lead time: 4–6 weeks from signed PO for a reserved 6-GPU pool in US-West (standard queue).
- Expedited path: we offer a 7–10 business day acceleration for a one-time provisioning fee and priority scheduling (used by several enterprise customers).
- Milestones we track: PO received -> billing token issued -> infra reservation -> image bake -> smoke tests -> handover. We will provide a milestone table and expected ETA after PO.

2) SLA credits calculation and cap
- Credits: calculated as a percentage of the monthly recurring fee for the affected SKU based on minutes of downtime beyond the SLA window. We will provide the exact formula in the term sheet; typical credit bands are: 99.9% = 10% credit, 99.5% = 25% credit, <99.5% = 50% credit (per-month cap 50%).
- Remedy timeline: initial remediation acknowledgement within 60 minutes for Sev1, full incident report within 72 hours.

3) Escrow and IP access
- We can do a binary escrow with a neutral agent (we've used Ironclad Escrow previously). Full source escrow is possible but requires additional paperwork and would be limited to extraordinary continuity triggers (bankruptcy, extended insolvency).
- Proposed language: binary escrow deliverable + release triggers tied to insolvency or persistent inability to meet SLAs for 90 days. We won't accept a release for ordinary contract termination.

4) Billing / invoicing cadence
- We support PO-based monthly invoicing and can accept net-45 with an approved credit application.
- Split invoicing: supported for multi-sku deals (we can accept separate POs per sku) but need invoicing contacts and PO references at activation.

Attachments: azure-privateplan-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term highlights)

Next steps
- I'll loop in legal (Olga) to review the proposed escrow/credit language. Can we target an alignment call next Tue 11/2 or Wed 11/3? If you prefer, we can exchange redline doc first.

Best,

Markus Klein
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Markus / Olga / Marissa — quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the term sheet you sent: 

- SLA credits: The banding you listed is fine but procurement wants to confirm whether credits are applied pro-rata across impacted SKUs or only to the subset of capacity types affected (e.g., if a single GPU type in the pool is impacted). We also want the mechanics (credit issued automatically vs. customer claim).

- Escrow triggers: Your 90-day persistent inability to meet SLAs looks reasonable. Legal is pushing for a narrow definition of "inability to meet" (we proposed 2 consecutive months below 99.5%). Will Redwood accept that narrower trigger?

- Billing: Net-45 is acceptable but we need invoice acceptance steps and a single consolidated invoice for the umbrella commitment (Altair prefers one invoice).

I've attached an initial redline of the term sheet from our counsel — file: Altair_Redlines_DRAFT.pdf. Please treat as work-in-progress.

Subject: Re: Altair Health — Azure Private Plan: delivery windows, SLA credits & escrow

Tom / Dana — thanks for the redline. Olga and I reviewed the key asks; answers below and a path forward.

- SLA credit mechanics
  - Credits apply pro-rata to the affected SKU(s) only (we will not reduce credits for unrelated SKUs). Credits are issued automatically once an incident is validated by Redwood (we surface incident transcripts in the Console and record the credit in the monthly invoice).
  - We can add a monthly cap of 50% of the affected SKU monthly fee (as noted).

- Escrow triggers
  - We can accept the narrower trigger you proposed: two consecutive months below 99.5% constitutes a releaseable continuity event, provided we retain the carve-out that a release requires (i) insolvency OR (ii) persistent inability as defined. We'll add language limiting release to a custodial/escrow process and require joint confirmation from both companies' CTOs before distribution.

- Billing / consolidated invoice
  - We can produce a single consolidated invoice for the umbrella commitment. Please provide the PO reference and the billing contact details (name, email, remit address).

Concessions / asks from Redwood
- We will accelerate provisioning to 10 business days for an implementation fee (to be listed in SOW).
- We request a 6-month minimum commitment on reserved capacity to enable the expedited scheduling (standard for accelerated provisioning).

Next steps
- Olga will take the proposed redline and produce a clean markup that captures the narrow escrow trigger and the consolidated invoice language.
- If Altair is OK with the 6-month minimum for expedited provisioning, we will prepare ALT-SOW-v3.docx and a final term sheet for signature.

Attachments: ALT-SOW-v3.docx, azure-privatesku-exhibit.pdf

I'll set a short call for Thurs 11/5 to confirm final edits unless you prefer to finish by exchange of redlines.

Thanks,
